note: A single red indicator on a power brick behind a monitor, in near-total darkness (roomLevel 0), surrounded by coiled orange ethernet cable. One LED, found and named RED at hue 1.3 with saturation 0.88. The cable is the interesting negative: it fills a third of the frame, it is strongly orange, and it is NOT bright enough to clip, so the emitter rule drops all of it. There is a second, dimmer red spot just below the LED - its own reflection on the plastic - which is dropped as too small. A reflection of an LED is, to the camera, an LED, so that is luck rather than judgement, and it is the reason the drop counters are printed in the footer. EXTRAS: at loose only, two faint spots on the orange cable coil. Ratchet at today's count. SINCE: those two were not spots on the cable, they were the SAME LED. One red light broke into three components - the clipped core at (390,649) area 39, a halo fragment 7px away, and another 31px away, all at hue 1.4-1.8. 31px is also the spacing of real LEDs on the router panels, so this is the capture that proved distance cannot decide it and the dark gap between two blobs can. All three now collapse to one; budget removed.
